adoption: Not adopted by states directly. Most state computer science standards are derived from these and from the K-12 CS Framework they share.
code_help: 2-AP-13 reads as: level 2 (grades 6-8), Algorithms and Programming, standard 13. Levels are 1A (K-2), 1B (3-5), 2 (6-8), 3A (9-10), and 3B (11-12 specialist).

standards.summary: Suggest improvements to a device's design after watching how people actually use it.
Build something that combines hardware and software to collect or exchange data.
Track down and fix faults in a device methodically, rather than by guessing.
Model how data is broken into pieces and reassembled when sent over a network.
Explain the trade-offs in keeping information secure.
Show how the same information can be stored and represented in different ways.
Collect data, then clean and organise it so it can be used.
Draw a conclusion from data and back it up.
Compare two ways of solving the same problem and say which is better, and why.
Use variables to hold and change data inside a program.
Control what a program does with loops, conditions, and repeated steps.
Break a problem into smaller named pieces that can be reused.
Plan a project in stages and keep track of what is done.
Build on somebody else's code or ideas, and credit them for it.
Test a program on purpose to find where it breaks, then fix it.
Write down how a program works so somebody else can follow it.
Talk about how computing has changed the way people live and work.
Explain how hardware and software work together to run a program.
Work through a fault systematically using a repeatable process.
Break a big problem down into parts small enough to solve one at a time.
Test and refine a program the way a professional would.
Judge and improve a program for correctness, readability, and usability.
